clarity.justification: The procedure closely matches the three hypotheses: it trains a probe to test shared encoding, measures whether "high-deference framing raises sycophancy/compliance," and tests whether English-side behavior "tracks the source-language status framing." The predictions are directional, and the stated null—"LLMs ignore honorific status, or it is cleanly compartmentalized with no leakage or behavioral effect"—provides an obvious refuting outcome, although no numeric decision thresholds distinguish meaningful transfer, leakage, or causal effects from noise. The main ambiguity is that "high-deference" means the user addresses the model as superior, whereas the hypothesis also glosses deferential input as "positions the user as high-status," leaving speaker status, addressee status, and politeness partly conflated. The approximately "600 base items," three framing conditions, chance baselines, within-content contrasts, and specificity measures make the intended comparisons concrete despite that construct-labeling issue.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is to "use activation patching to localize where the status signal is computed" and derive a shared direction suitable for steering across languages; this requires custom layer/token sweeps but is a standard residual-stream intervention rather than an undefined magic step. The named Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Aya-23-8B, and Gemma-2-9B artifacts exist, and activation extraction, logistic probes, PCA/CCA, forward-hook patching, and vector steering are supported by ordinary Hugging Face/PyTorch and interpretability tooling. Resources and scale are usefully quantified as "~600 base items," three conditions, eight languages, and four models, while the proposal explains how to construct and verify the new multilingual stimulus set rather than assuming it already exists. Negative outcomes are runnable because the design includes plain and low-status contrasts, chance and in-language probe baselines, an "English-embedded control," unrelated-task and factual-accuracy specificity controls, held-out constructions, and base-versus-instruct comparisons.
